items.title: Vincent Pelote interviewed by Monk Rowe, Orlando, Florida, February 25, 2017
items.q: In fact I had a guitar teacher, Remo Palmier, who said to me, “I don’t do that four to the bar nonsense.”

ctx.x: It’s almost better that they don’t know that it doesn’t fit. Because if they know it doesn’t fit then I think they’re making a bad musical decision.

But it’s almost like if you take them to task then you also have to sort of take the drummer to task. Because chances are the drummers in those bands weren’t keeping time on the hi hat, they were probably using the bass drum more. And it’s a whole different feel actually. I don’t think anybody today really knows how those drummers felt time. The bop thing has taken over. So everybody plays like a bop drummer now, even the swing guys. So that’s just the way it is. Even the bass players are pushing more than they…

back now. I think they pushed more in those days. They were more in your face. And of course you could hardly find any guitarists that wanted to just play rhythm. They just don’t want to do that. In fact I had a guitar teacher, Remo Palmier, who said to me, “I don’t do that four to the bar nonsense.”
